title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
authors: Alec Radford, Jong Wook Kim, Chris Hallacy, Aditya Ramesh, Gabriel Goh, Sandhini Agarwal, Girish Sastry, Amanda Askell, Pamela Mishkin, Jack Clark, Gretchen Krueger, Ilya Sutskever
annotation: The seminal paper introducing CLIP, establishing contrastive pretraining on 400 million image-text pairs for zero-shot visual transfer and open-vocabulary recognition.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
authors: Edward J. Hu, Yelong Shen, Phillip Wallis, Zeyuan Allen-Zhu, Yuanzhi Li, Shean Wang, Lu Wang, Weizhu Chen
annotation: Proposes Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), freezing pretrained weights and injecting trainable rank decomposition matrices, reducing trainable parameters by over 98% with zero inference latency overhead.

title: DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision
authors: Maxime Oquab, Timothee Darcet, Theo Moutakanni, Huy Vo, Marc Szafraniec, Vasil Khalidov, Pierre Fernandez, Daniel Haziza, Francisco Massa, Alaaeldin El-Nouby, Russell Howes, Po-Yao Huang, Hu Xu, Vasu Sharma, Shang-Wen Li, Jaemin Cho, Mido Assran, Nicolas Ballas, Gabriel Synnaeve, Mark Tygert, Saurabh Goyal, Hazem Vadera, Jiabo Hu, Patrick Labatut, Armand Joulin, Piotr Dollar
annotation: Demonstrates that discriminative self-supervised pretraining at scale produces universal visual features exhibiting emergent segmentation and powerful zero-shot linear probe properties.

title: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners
authors: Kaiming He, Xinlei Chen, Saining Xie, Yanghao Li, Piotr Dollar, Ross Girshick
publisher: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
annotation: Introduces Masked Autoencoders (MAE), demonstrating that reconstructing high-ratio (75%) masked image patches enables highly scalable self-supervised representation learning for vision transformers.
